## Question 1

- Describe what it means for to be the maximum likelihood estimator.

- What are properties of MLEs?

## Question 2

::: question
Explain why

$\lim_{n \rightarrow \infty}Var(\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}) = 0$ and $\lim_{n \rightarrow \infty} Bias(\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}) = 0$ means that $\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}$ is a consistent estimator.
:::

## Question 3

::: question
You are fitting a regression model to predict insurance costs based on patient demographics, prior history of medical diagnoses, and other information. You identify 5 observations that have leverage values greater than $2(p+1)/n$. You consider removing these observations from the analysis data.

Before deciding whether to remove them, what two pieces of information would you want to examine, and how would each piece of information affect your decision?
:::

## Question 4

Let's go back to [data](20-logistic-regression.html#/risk-of-coronary-heart-disease) collected in Framingham, MA to study the risk of coronary heart disease. A two-way table of the relationship between education and being high risk for heart disease is below.


::: {.cell layout-align="center"}
::: {.cell-output-display}


|Education | Not High Risk| High Risk|
|:---------|-------------:|---------:|
|1         |          1397|       323|
|2         |          1106|       147|
|3         |           601|        88|
|4         |           403|        70|


:::
:::


## Question 4

::: question
a.  What is the probability a randomly selected individual with education level 4 (College) is high risk for heart disease?

b.  What are the odds for this individual?

c.  How do the odds of being high risk for an individual with education level 4 (College) compare to the odds for an individual from education level 1 (Some High School)?
:::

## Question 6

::: question
Suppose you fit a simple linear regression model.

a.  Draw a scatterplot that contains an observation with high leverage but low Cook’s distance.

b.  Draw a scatterplot that contains an observation with high leverage and high Cook’s distance.

c.  Draw a scatterplot that contains an observation with a large magnitude standardized residual.
:::

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
